input.raw_text: Fourth down and long again. The S&P is down high single digits for December alone and sits barely a percent above an official bear market, with small caps already there. The Fed hiked last week and the dot plot still shows two more moves next year, while Powell's long-way-from-neutral line keeps getting replayed on the tape; the curve is within a whisker of its flattest since 2007, and the front end is pricing a hike priced out, not in. Oil has simply collapsed. The tech names that carried this market all year lead the way down — Apple is off about a third from its highs on supply-chain and China jitters, and the FAANG complex as a whole has corrected into bear-market territory. Clients keep asking about a Santa rally and I keep telling them: volume is thin, morale is worse, and nothing is buying the dips.
input.summary: U.S. equities are under severe December pressure, with the S&P 500 approaching bear-market territory and small caps already there. Recent Federal Reserve tightening, expectations for further moves, and an exceptionally flat yield curve accompany weaker front-end expectations. Oil has fallen sharply, while technology leaders, including Apple and the broader FAANG complex, are leading equity declines. Thin volume, poor sentiment, and absent dip demand leave prospects for a seasonal rebound uncertain.
